there are states in the US that only allow liquor sales in State run locations. North Carolina is one such example. They are called ABC stores if I recall correctly.

Not only are "blue" laws ridiculous, it's amazing how many 'average' people will defend them for no apparent reason.

These laws shit on anyone who works second or third shift, they slow commerce and the economy, and in the end all they really are for your average person is a mild inconvenience. So long as you are aware of the law you just go out a little earlier and get the booze.

I am in the wine and spirits industry selling to 47 states and 7 countries. State liquor laws are absolutely the most frustrating part of my job. Most of these laws aren't necessarily "blue" laws but have been in place since prohibition to insure the mob retained their revenue stream after the volstead act was repealed. Some state's are just absolutely ridiculous. In Pennsylvania for example their wine and spirits are completely state run and every buying decision is made by one man called "the general." Salesman will go in there to try to get a placement with their heads bowed begging like he is a king. I went once and will never attempt to sell anything in the state again. In Ohio, BY LAW, the retailer must make 33.3% margin and the distributor must make 25% margin. So say as a producer I sell a case of wine for $100 in Ohio, it has to hit the shelf at $200 by law. So for the items I sell as national programs to chains, if they operate in Ohio, I will end up losing money on every bottle of wine they sell in Ohio so they can hit a national price point.

There isnt a state without a fucked up liquor law and it breaks a libertarians heart having to deal with it.
